\subsection*{Randomized --- Zero PPIT: Results}

\begin{definition}[Polynomial identity testing language]
\lean{Randomized.PITLang}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p013-b004,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p016-b002
}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p004-b003}
\label{Randomized.PITLang}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.AlgCircuit, Randomized.AlgCircuit.WellFormed, Randomized.AlgCircuit.encode, Randomized.AlgCircuit.toMvPolynomial, Turing.pairEncode}
The language consists of Boolean strings that encode a pair of algebraic circuits over
the same number of variables, where both circuits are well formed and compute the same
multivariate polynomial.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Polynomial identity testing verifier]
\lean{Randomized.pitVerifier}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p016-b003,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p017-b003
}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{
  pdf-26d95080dbde-p005-b001,
  pdf-26d95080dbde-p005-b002,
  pdf-26d95080dbde-p005-b003,
  pdf-26d95080dbde-p005-b004
}
\label{Randomized.pitVerifier}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Randomized.AlgCircuit.WellFormed, Randomized.AlgCircuit.decode, Randomized.AlgCircuit.subCircuit, Randomized.AlgCircuit.zeroTest}
Given Boolean lists $x$ and $r$, decode the two components of the pair encoded by $x$.
The verifier returns false exactly when both decode as well-formed algebraic circuits
over the same number of variables and the difference of their outputs evaluates to zero
on $r$; in every other case it returns true.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Verifier Evaluation After Decoding]
\lean{Randomized.pitVerifier_of_decode}
\label{Randomized.pitVerifier_of_decode}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Randomized.AlgCircuit, Randomized.AlgCircuit.WellFormed, Randomized.AlgCircuit.decode, Randomized.AlgCircuit.subCircuit, Randomized.AlgCircuit.zeroTest, Randomized.pitVerifier}
\difficulty{1}
Let $x$ and $r$ be bit strings, let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $C,C'$ be arithmetic
circuits with $n$ input variables. Suppose the total first and second projections of $x$
decode to $C$ and $C'$, respectively. The verifier on $x$ and $r$ equals false exactly
when both circuits are well formed and the zero test on the circuit representing their
difference returns true; if either circuit is not well formed, the verifier returns
true.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Verifier on Invalid Circuit Pairs]
\lean{Randomized.pitVerifier_of_not}
\label{Randomized.pitVerifier_of_not}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Randomized.AlgCircuit, Randomized.AlgCircuit.WellFormed, Randomized.AlgCircuit.decode, Randomized.pitVerifier}
\difficulty{5}
Let $x,r$ be bit strings. If there do not exist a natural number $n$ and two well-formed
arithmetic circuits with $n$ input variables to which the total first and second
projections of $x$ decode, then the verifier on $x$ and $r$ returns true.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Pair decoding recovers the input encoding]
\lean{Randomized.eq_pairEncode_of_decode}
\label{Randomized.eq_pairEncode_of_decode}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Randomized.AlgCircuit, Randomized.AlgCircuit.decode, Turing.eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode, Turing.pairDecode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ be a binary string and let $c$ be a dimension together with an algebraic circuit
of that dimension. If decoding the first component of the pair parser’s total
projections of $x$ returns $c$, then $x$ is the self-delimiting encoding of those two
projections.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Characterization of the Polynomial Identity Testing Language]
\lean{Randomized.mem_PITLang_iff}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p013-b004,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p016-b002
}
\label{Randomized.mem_PITLang_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Randomized.AlgCircuit, Randomized.AlgCircuit.WellFormed, Randomized.AlgCircuit.decode, Randomized.AlgCircuit.decode_encode, Randomized.AlgCircuit.encode_of_decode, Randomized.AlgCircuit.toMvPolynomial, Randomized.PITLang, Randomized.eq_pairEncode_of_decode}
\difficulty{4}
A bit string $x$ belongs to the language of polynomial identity testing exactly when it
can be parsed as a pair of encodings of well-formed algebraic circuits with the same
number of input variables, and the polynomials computed by those circuits over the
integers are equal.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Polynomial identity test witness predicate]
\lean{Randomized.PIT.pitW}
\label{Randomized.PIT.pitW}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.uHead, Complexity.BinArith.uRest, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Randomized.PIT.pipe, Randomized.PIT.sI, Randomized.PIT.scanRun, Randomized.PIT.validW, Turing.pairEncode}
For a Boolean list $z$, let $a$ and $b$ be the first components obtained by applying the
pair decoder twice to $z$. The predicate returns true exactly when either $a$ or $b$ is
not a valid witness, their encoded head lengths differ, or the pipeline rejects the
nested pair encoding formed from their heads, scan results, tails, and the final bit
$1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-Time Computability of the PIT Predicate]
\lean{Randomized.PIT.polyTimeComputable_pitW}
\label{Randomized.PIT.polyTimeComputable_pitW}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_app, Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_slot3, Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_test_app, Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_uHead, Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_uRest, Complexity.BinArith.uHead, Complexity.BinArith.uRest, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.append, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.comp, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairFstD_pairEncode, Complexity.pairSndD, Complexity.pairSndD_pairEncode, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_and, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_const, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_lenEq, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_not, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_or, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairFstD, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairSndD, Randomized.PIT.pitW, Randomized.PIT.polyTimeComputable_pipe, Randomized.PIT.polyTimeComputable_scanRun, Randomized.PIT.polyTimeComputable_validW, Randomized.PIT.sI, Randomized.PIT.scanRun, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{5}
The Boolean function on finite bit strings that sends each string $z$ to the one-bit
string whose bit is $	exttt{pitW}(z)$ is computable by a deterministic Turing machine in
time $C(n+1)^c$ on every input of length $n$, for some natural numbers $C$ and $c$.
\end{theorem}

\proofstep
  {Randomized.eff_pitVerifier}
  {context}
  {arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}
  {pdf-26d95080dbde-p003-b004,
    pdf-26d95080dbde-p005-b003,
    pdf-26d95080dbde-p005-b004}
A polynomial identity testing instance is a pair of nonempty, well-formed arithmetic
circuits over the integers with the same number of input variables, whose computed
polynomials are equal; encode the pair by doubling each bit of the first circuit code,
appending the separator $01$, and then the second code. The language of such encodings
belongs to coRP: there is a polynomial-time randomized verifier that always rejects an
identity and accepts every string outside this language with probability at least $2/3$.
\end{theorem}

The language of bit strings encoding pairs of well-formed arithmetic circuits over the
integers, with the same number of variables, whose associated multivariate polynomials
are equal, belongs to BPP.
\end{theorem}

  {Randomized.inCoRP_PITLang}
  {context}
  {arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}
  {pdf-26d95080dbde-p005-b001,
    pdf-26d95080dbde-p005-b002,
    pdf-26d95080dbde-p005-b004,
    pdf-26d95080dbde-p006-b004}
The language of paired encodings of two well-formed algebraic circuits on the same
number of inputs whose associated integer polynomials are equal belongs to co-RP with
polynomial time bound, where acceptance is certain on inputs outside the language and
the probability of outputting true is at least $2/3$ on inputs in the language.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-26d95080dbde-p006-b004,
    pdf-26d95080dbde-p002-b003}
The language of paired encodings of two well-formed algebraic circuits on the same
number of inputs whose associated integer polynomials are equal belongs to bounded-error
probabilistic polynomial time, with the class defined using finite nondeterministic
machines driven by uniformly random choice bits and acceptance probability at least
$2/3$.
\end{theorem}
